game: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine (1993, Mega Drive/Genesis)
target: Spoiler-free full-system completion of the original USA cartridge: every mode, setting, difficulty route, board mechanic, score system, helper event, easter egg, and preservation experiment

areas.name: Cartridge Route and Safeguards
areas.location_cue: The dark-blue title screen and vine-framed menu before a board is opened.
areas.note: Confirm the selected build and protect progress before exploring every mode.

save_backup.title: Create an untouched title state
save_backup.why: The cartridge has no internal save memory.
save_backup.detail: Keep one title state plus separate rolling states; never overwrite the only state while testing passwords or hidden menus.

point_of_no_return.title: Power-off erases volatile records
point_of_no_return.why: Scenario progress is represented by passwords, while score tables live only in powered memory.
point_of_no_return.detail: Photograph or transcribe every new password and record any wanted score before closing the emulator.

levels.1: Confirm the preserved build before tracking completion.
levels.2: Use the original NTSC-U Mega Drive/Genesis cartridge in the selected archive.
levels.3: Verify a 1,048,576-byte ROM with SHA-1 AA6B60103FA92BC95FCC824BF1675E411627C8D3. Keep the separate eight-bit release for its own Puzzle Mode guide.

levels.1: Keep a safe return point before entering menus.
levels.2: Make a state on the title screen after the opening logos.
levels.3: Store it in a protected slot, then use different slots for active play. This preserves a clean route for demonstrations, secrets, and settings checks.

levels.1: Treat each victory screen as a save opportunity.
levels.2: Record the four-bean password whenever Scenario awards one.
levels.3: Write the difficulty beside the four symbols because the same position uses different passwords across settings. Passwords restore position but never the accumulated score.

levels.1: Important records disappear with the powered session.
levels.2: Capture the score table before closing or resetting the cartridge.
levels.3: Enter up to three initials when a result reaches the top five, then save a screenshot or note. A later cold boot clears those entries.

levels.1: A related version contains material missing here.
levels.2: Do not expect Puzzle Mode in this Mega Drive cartridge.
levels.3: Complete this 16-bit guide independently. The Game Gear archive entry receives its own guide because its thirty fixed puzzles are absent here.

levels.1: Let the title screen remain untouched briefly.
levels.2: Wait at the title screen until the automatic explanation and demonstration begin.
levels.3: Do not press Start after the title settles. Let the introductory sequence and its playable-rule demonstration run through before returning to the menu.

areas.name: Core Board Rules
areas.location_cue: A paired-bean board with a central preview meter and two opposing wells.
areas.note: Master every stable input and board interaction before the difficulty routes.

save_backup.title: Save before controlled practice
save_backup.why: A failed board can interrupt a specific mechanic test.
save_backup.detail: Use separate Exercise states for rotation, splitting, chaining, garbage clearing, and the loss-column check.

point_of_no_return.title: The centre-top cell ends a board
point_of_no_return.why: A stack entering the third column's top position immediately collapses that side.
point_of_no_return.detail: Test the boundary only on a disposable state, then reload rather than losing useful route progress.

levels.1: Learn horizontal placement before relying on speed.
levels.2: Move with Left or Right and hold Down to increase the current pair's fall rate.
levels.3: Guide a falling pair between the six columns with Left or Right. Hold Down only after alignment; it accelerates descent and adds a small score for each forced step.

levels.1: Use both rotation directions to avoid extra movement.
levels.2: Press A or C for clockwise rotation and B for counter-clockwise rotation.
levels.3: Practice returning a vertical pair to horizontal with either direction. Confirm the mapped buttons in Options if all three face buttons do not rotate as expected.

levels.1: There is a dedicated interruption control.
levels.2: Press Start during a board to pause, then press it again to resume.
levels.3: Use Start only after the falling pair is positioned. Resume deliberately so an accelerated or poorly aligned pair does not lock unexpectedly.

levels.1: Build a compact group without using diagonals.
levels.2: Join at least four same-colour beans through shared sides.
levels.3: Make a vertical, horizontal, L-shaped, T-shaped, or clustered group of four or more. Corner-only contact does not connect the group and will not clear.

items.label: Split a Pair on Uneven Ground

levels.1: A horizontal landing can separate its two halves.
levels.2: Place a horizontal pair across columns with different stack heights.
levels.3: Land one half on the taller column; the unsupported bean drops to the lower available cell. Use this to feed a buried colour without blocking its neighbour.

levels.1: Arrange one clear to complete another below.
levels.2: Remove a supporting group so the beans above fall into a second match.
levels.3: Build the later match first, separate one required colour with a supporting group, then clear that support. The fall completes the next group and counts as another chain link.

levels.1: Clear colour beside the unmatchable pieces.
levels.2: Make a normal four-bean clear directly adjacent to Refugee Beans.
levels.3: Refugee Beans cannot match with one another. Clear any qualifying coloured group touching them by an edge; every adjacent Refugee disappears with that clear.

levels.1: Plan one placement beyond the active pair.
levels.2: Read the paired colours displayed between the two boards.
levels.3: Before locking the current pair, reserve a column or support for the previewed colours. Recheck the meter after each lock because it advances immediately.

levels.1: The whole top edge is not equally dangerous.
levels.2: Observe the third column from the left at the board's ceiling.
levels.3: Use a disposable Exercise state and fill that column until a piece occupies its top entry cell. The board ends even if neighbouring columns still have open space.

areas.name: Scoring and Chain Mastery
areas.location_cue: An active board with a rising numeric score and linked groups prepared beneath the falling pair.
areas.note: Record the scoring behaviours and advanced clears needed for a genuine full-system run.

save_backup.title: Keep a pre-chain state
save_backup.why: Random pairs can make a carefully prepared scoring test difficult to repeat.
save_backup.detail: Save immediately before the trigger piece, then replay the same setup while checking group size, chain depth, and resulting score.

point_of_no_return.title: A board loss ends the attempt
point_of_no_return.why: Exercise scoring continues only while the board remains open.
point_of_no_return.detail: Capture the score and cleared-bean total before deliberately testing the loss condition.

levels.1: Turn safe descent distance into small points.
levels.2: Hold Down after positioning a falling pair and watch the score rise during its descent.
levels.3: Start from an empty upper board, align first, then hold Down through several cells. Repeat without sacrificing placement; each forced step contributes a small amount.

levels.1: A larger same-colour cluster carries a multiplier.
levels.2: Connect five or more matching beans in one simultaneous clear.
levels.3: Prepare an oversized orthogonal group and complete it with one drop. Compare its score with an ordinary four-clear; excess beans raise the group multiplier.

levels.1: Use gravity to trigger a second colour.
levels.2: Clear a lower support so the falling beans complete another group.
levels.3: Prepare the upper group with one missing connection, support it above a ready lower clear, then trigger the lower colour. Confirm two separate clear flashes before rebuilding.

levels.1: Extend the same gravity logic through several colours.
levels.2: Stack staggered triggers so each clear completes the next prepared group.
levels.3: Work backward from the final colour, giving every layer exactly one delayed connection. Trigger the lowest support and confirm at least four successive clears without another input.

levels.1: A quick board awards more than clear points.
levels.2: Win a Scenario match before its time-bonus window expires.
levels.3: Open with a compact chain and send disruptive Refugees early. Finish within 129 seconds; at 130 seconds or later the separate time award is zero.

levels.1: Leave no coloured or helper bean behind.
levels.2: Arrange Exercise Mode so one chain empties every occupied cell.
levels.3: Build from one side and avoid isolated colours beneath the structure. Trigger the chain only when every remaining bean participates; the game adds an empty-board bonus scaled by the current level.

levels.1: Exercise Mode preserves a session-only ranking.
levels.2: Finish an Exercise attempt with a score high enough for the top five.
levels.3: After the board ends, wait without pressing anything for roughly ten seconds. When the ranking screen appears, enter three initials and capture the table before power-off.

areas.name: Options and Controller Audit
areas.location_cue: The vine-bordered Options panel reached from the main mode list.
areas.note: Exercise every configurable cartridge setting and both controller paths.

save_backup.title: Save the default options first
save_backup.why: Changing inputs or match rules can make later tests appear broken.
save_backup.detail: Record the original values in one state, then use a disposable Options state for the full configuration audit.

point_of_no_return.title: Leaving Options applies the changes
point_of_no_return.why: The next board uses the currently selected assignments, difficulty, match count, and sampling state.
point_of_no_return.detail: Restore the intended route values before beginning any scored Scenario or versus record.

levels.1: Confirm every face-button assignment can change.
levels.2: Use Key Assignment with controller one and alter A, B, and C.
levels.3: Assign at least one clockwise and one counter-clockwise input, enter a practice board, test both rotations, then restore the preferred layout.

levels.1: The second pad has an independent mapping.
levels.2: Use controller two on Key Assignment and change its A, B, and C functions.
levels.3: Connect the second controller before opening Options. Make and test a reversible mapping in versus or Exercise, then return both pads to the chosen layout.

levels.1: Scenario has four independent challenge settings.
levels.2: Cycle VS COM Level through Easy, Normal, Hard, and Hardest.
levels.3: Record all four values in Options and begin a separate Scenario route on each. Passwords are difficulty-specific, so do not reuse a code under the wrong setting.

levels.1: The head-to-head series length is configurable.
levels.2: Cycle the versus setting through 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, and 15 games.
levels.3: Change 1P VS. 2P Mode in Options and enter a match after each value. The required majority scales from one win through eight wins.

levels.1: One switch controls the short match voices.
levels.2: Set Sampling off and on, then enter a versus-style board under each value.
levels.3: Use the same opening actions on both tests. Confirm the voice samples disappear when disabled and return when enabled, then leave the preferred setting active.

levels.1: Check both pads before a long versus series.
levels.2: Open Input Test and press every direction plus A, B, C, and Start on each controller.
levels.3: Confirm every displayed input changes once without sticking. When finished, press A and Start together to return to the Options panel.

areas.name: Scenario Boards
areas.location_cue: Successive two-well puzzle boards reached from Scenario Start or the four-symbol Continue screen.
areas.note: Complete every mechanical difficulty route while revealing no opponent or closing identity in advance.

save_backup.title: Save before each new board
save_backup.why: A loss can consume time and a password restores position but not score.
save_backup.detail: Keep a rolling pre-board state and the displayed four-symbol password in a difficulty-labelled log.

point_of_no_return.title: The final clear advances immediately
point_of_no_return.why: There is no post-win free movement or later chance to reconstruct the completed score route.
point_of_no_return.detail: Capture the result and allow the closing presentation to finish before reset, difficulty changes, or another password test.

levels.1: Begin with the gentlest CPU setting.
levels.2: Set VS COM Level to Easy before selecting Scenario Start.
levels.3: Clear the entire uninterrupted route on Easy, logging each awarded password. After the completion sequence begins, capture proof and keep the final pre-match state.

levels.1: Repeat the route at its standard challenge.
levels.2: Set VS COM Level to Normal and begin a separate Scenario Start run.
levels.3: Use a distinct state and password log from Easy. Clear every board on Normal and capture the completed route before changing the difficulty again.

levels.1: The faster route rewards earlier disruption.
levels.2: Set VS COM Level to Hard before opening a fresh Scenario route.
levels.3: Prioritize reliable two- and three-chains, protect the third column, and log Hard-specific passwords. Confirm the full completion sequence before moving to Hardest.

levels.1: Reserve the maximum CPU setting for a prepared run.
levels.2: Set VS COM Level to Hardest and begin from Scenario Start.
levels.3: Keep a state before every board, use compact pre-planned chains, and record the difficulty-specific passwords. Finish the complete route without substituting a lower-setting password.

levels.1: The continue screen accepts four bean symbols.
levels.2: Select Scenario, choose Continue, and enter a password recorded under the current difficulty.
levels.3: Match the Options difficulty to the log, enter all four symbols, then press Start or select End and confirm with A or C. Verify the expected board before overwriting any state.

levels.1: Watch for fast placements concentrated into one or two colours.
levels.2: Keep a flat board and prepare a simple two-chain while the CPU places erratically.
levels.3: Do not race each small clear. Build a compact two-link chain across the centre, trigger before your loss column rises, and use the first Refugees to break the opponent's narrow colour plan.

levels.1: An early board repeatedly prepares a four-bean row.
levels.2: Send a small attack before that neat row becomes a chain foundation.
levels.3: Build vertically near the sides and fire a two-chain as soon as it is stable. Even a modest Refugee drop interrupts the opponent's horizontal four pattern and delays its follow-up.

levels.1: This board removes tidy groups rapidly but rarely chains deeply.
levels.2: Prepare one stronger chain instead of matching its steady single clears.
levels.3: Keep your trigger column open and construct a three-link staircase. Launch it before the centre rises; several waves of Refugees overpower repeated single clears more reliably than trading them one-for-one.

levels.1: Both outer columns begin climbing while the centre stays open.
levels.2: Attack the exposed centre before the side towers become useful.
levels.3: Use the breathing room to assemble a two- or three-chain around your middle columns. Trigger early; Refugees landing through the centre make the two tall edge structures harder for the CPU to connect.

levels.1: Expect fast same-colour removals alongside two edge stacks.
levels.2: Build a short chain before the opponent stabilizes both sides.
levels.3: Keep your own loss column low, assemble a reliable two-chain, and release it as the CPU begins extending its second edge. The interruption matters more than waiting for a perfect large attack.

levels.1: The opposing stack remains broad and low.
levels.2: Send several attacks without allowing a recovery interval.
levels.3: Use compact two-chains in succession. A low spread absorbs one drop well, so prepare the next trigger before firing the first and keep Refugees arriving faster than the board can clear them.

levels.1: The opposing board spends time preparing a larger chain.
levels.2: Fire first and scatter Refugees through its planned structure.
levels.3: Choose speed over maximum size: finish a dependable two- or three-chain while the CPU is still arranging colours, then trigger immediately. The scattered Refugees sever the prepared links.

levels.1: Pairs are placed and matched with little delay.
levels.2: Protect the loss column and use efficient compact chains.
levels.3: Avoid tall speculative structures. Build horizontally across safer columns, keep the third column open, and send a clean two-chain whenever the opponent's board begins accepting new Refugees.

levels.1: Expect frequent small chains rather than one large attack.
levels.2: Counter with a deeper prepared chain after stabilizing incoming Refugees.
levels.3: Clear immediate danger beside coloured groups, then rebuild from a low base. Hold a three-link trigger until the opponent finishes a short attack, and return one larger wave during its recovery.

levels.1: The other board combines vertical stacks with modest chains.
levels.2: Strike the tower bases before the stacks connect cleanly.
levels.3: Use side columns for your build and leave the loss column shallow. Trigger two compact chains close together; uneven Refugee placement around the tower bases blocks the CPU's planned joins.

levels.1: Chain structures develop on both outer sides.
levels.2: Attack the centre and preserve room for counter-clears.
levels.3: Keep matching colours beside likely Refugee landing cells. Launch an early chain through the middle, then clear incoming pieces locally; do not copy the opponent's risky two-sided height.

levels.1: Large chain structures appear with very little setup time.
levels.2: Use an immediate small attack, then prepare the stronger follow-up.
levels.3: Open with the fastest safe two-chain you can form. While its Refugees disrupt the other board, extend a second structure; waiting for one perfect chain usually gives the opponent the first attack.

levels.1: The falling pairs arrive at the route's highest pace.
levels.2: Minimize rotations and pre-plan from the centre preview.
levels.3: Read the next pair before the active one locks, keep the third column below its neighbours, and favour short dependable chains. Use passwords or a pre-board state for retries rather than rebuilding earlier progress.

levels.1: Let the post-board sequence finish without skipping.
levels.2: After the decisive victory, keep the controller idle and watch through the complete closing presentation.
levels.3: Do not reset when the last board disappears. Capture the completion sequence and credits through their natural return, then label the evidence with the active CPU difficulty.

areas.name: Two-Player Versus
areas.location_cue: Two adjacent wells with separate controllers, difficulty selections, and victory stars.
areas.note: Exercise every handicap and series-length rule with two connected pads.

save_backup.title: Keep a two-controller setup state
save_backup.why: Controller assignment and match length are configured before the board opens.
save_backup.detail: Save after both pads pass Input Test, then branch states for each handicap and series-length check.

point_of_no_return.title: A round result starts a short timer
point_of_no_return.why: The losing side must confirm the next match before the rematch window closes.
point_of_no_return.detail: Capture the victory stars first, then press Start on the losing controller within ten seconds when continuing the series.

levels.1: Both players need independent pads before selection.
levels.2: Connect two controllers, select 1P VS. 2P Mode, and choose a level for each side.
levels.3: Confirm both pads in Input Test first. Player one controls the left board and player two the right; begin only after both difficulty choices are intentional.

levels.1: Begin with an empty, slow board.
levels.2: Select Easiest for at least one player in versus.
levels.3: Start with no prefilled rows and confirm the gentlest falling speed. Complete a round, then swap sides so both controllers are checked under this level.

levels.1: Increase speed without adding starting rows.
levels.2: Select Easy for at least one player in versus.
levels.3: Verify the board begins empty but falls faster than Easiest. Finish a round using the same chain pattern for a clean comparison.

levels.1: Use the fastest empty-board selection.
levels.2: Select Normal for at least one player in versus.
levels.3: Confirm an empty starting well and the third speed tier. Clear a round without changing the match-count option mid-series.

levels.1: This selection begins with a partial stack.
levels.2: Select Hard and inspect the three prefilled rows.
levels.3: Build above the three-row handicap without covering the loss column. Complete a round, then repeat on the opposite side to check both controllers.

levels.1: The maximum handicap leaves little free height.
levels.2: Select Hardest and inspect the five prefilled rows.
levels.3: Clear adjacent colours immediately and keep the third column low. Complete a round from the five-row start, then test the same level on the other side.

levels.1: Options provides eight odd-numbered match totals.
levels.2: Start a versus series at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, and 15 games.
levels.3: Change the setting in Options between tests. Enter each series and verify its majority target; for the longest setting, play until one side records eight stars.

levels.1: A finished round offers only a brief continuation choice.
levels.2: After a loss, press Start on the losing controller within ten seconds.
levels.3: Watch the victory star update, then confirm before the countdown expires. Also let one disposable test time out so the series-ending behaviour is documented.

areas.name: Exercise Mode
areas.location_cue: A single practice well, or two joined wells, without incoming Refugee attacks.
areas.note: Complete every starting level, helper event, score bonus, and multiplayer practice path.

save_backup.title: Keep states before helper events
save_backup.why: The helper path and available pairs vary during a long scoring attempt.
save_backup.detail: Save before the board becomes crowded, then branch attempts for recolouring, column clearing, empty-board, and high-score tests.

point_of_no_return.title: A filled loss column ends scoring
point_of_no_return.why: Helper appearances do not protect the board indefinitely.
point_of_no_return.detail: Capture any score milestone before allowing the third-column entry cell to fill.

levels.1: Begin from the plain practice setting.
levels.2: Select Easiest and start with no opening score bonus.
levels.3: Confirm the clean starting score and use the slower pace to demonstrate four-clears, split pairs, and a controlled two-link chain.

levels.1: The middle setting begins with a score grant.
levels.2: Select Normal and confirm a 40,000-point opening bonus.
levels.3: Record the initial score before placing a pair, then continue until falling speed increases and the recolouring helper appears.

levels.1: The highest setting begins further into progression.
levels.2: Select Hardest and confirm a 90,000-point opening bonus.
levels.3: Record the starting score, manage the faster board, and continue until the large helper appears. Preserve a state before testing its two-column path.

levels.1: Practice attacks do not cross between wells.
levels.2: Create chains in Exercise and verify no Refugee Beans arrive on the other board.
levels.3: Join a second player, trigger several chains on either side, and inspect both wells. Scores and speed rise independently without sending attack pieces.

levels.1: A second practice board can enter during play.
levels.2: Press Start on controller two while Exercise Mode is active.
levels.3: Connect and test the pad first, begin a one-player Exercise board, then press controller two's Start. Continue until both independent boards have completed a clear.

levels.1: The middle progression path introduces a moving helper.
levels.2: Continue Normal Exercise until the small helper crosses the board.
levels.3: Let it land on a coloured bean so the beans along its random path change to that colour and clear. In a separate attempt, let it reach the floor for 10,000 points.

levels.1: The high progression path introduces a heavier helper.
levels.2: Continue Hardest Exercise until the large green helper drops.
levels.3: Align its fall over occupied columns and watch it erase the two-column path. In a separate attempt, allow an unobstructed floor landing to collect 12,000 points.

levels.1: A long survival run can enter the local table.
levels.2: Build repeated chains until the result qualifies for a top-five position.
levels.3: After losing, wait roughly ten seconds without input, enter three initials, and photograph the table. Preserve it externally because a cold boot erases the cartridge record.

areas.name: Secrets and Preservation Experiments
areas.location_cue: The title logo, a live Scenario board with a second pad, and the normally hidden Options entry.
areas.note: Document every harmless easter egg, reproducible engine quirk, and inaccessible retained feature honestly.

save_backup.title: Branch from clean disposable states
save_backup.why: Region switching, cheat hardware, and timing tests should never touch the only completion state.
save_backup.detail: Duplicate the clean title state into separate slots before each secret or preservation experiment.

point_of_no_return.title: Hidden-menu access changes runtime conditions
point_of_no_return.why: The retained audio menu is blocked during ordinary play and needs an external access method.
point_of_no_return.detail: Record which method was used, then return to the unmodified USA route for normal completion evidence.

levels.1: Controller one animates part of the title.
levels.2: At the title screen, press A, B, and C separately on controller one.
levels.3: Wait until the full logo is stable. Press each face button once and confirm the three letters within “Mean” respond individually; capture all three reactions.

levels.1: A second pad controls the other word.
levels.2: At the title screen, press A, B, and C separately on controller two.
levels.3: Connect controller two before boot if necessary, let the title settle, then press its three face buttons. Confirm the letters within “Bean” react independently.

levels.1: A second controller can alter Scenario timing.
levels.2: During Scenario, hold Left or Right on the controller assigned to the CPU side.
levels.3: Use a disposable early-board state with two pads. Hold either horizontal direction on the opposite-side controller and compare CPU descent; the hold blocks its manual fast-drop input until released.

items.label: Open Sound Test with Game Genie

levels.1: The audio menu remains in the ROM but is blocked.
levels.2: Apply Game Genie code ADTT-AAAE, boot normally, and return to Options.
levels.3: Use a separate cheat-enabled cartridge session. Enter Options after boot and open the newly visible Sound Test; sample its music and effects, then disable the code before normal play.

items.label: Open Sound Test by Region Switching

levels.1: An emulator can expose the same retained menu.
levels.2: Boot as USA, wait past the Sega logo, then switch the running machine to Japanese region.
levels.3: Use a disposable emulator state and a core that permits live region changes. Switch only after the Sega logo, enter Options, inspect Sound Test, then reboot under USA before resuming completion.

levels.1: The hidden menu contains music not heard normally.
levels.2: Open Sound Test and step through every music and effects index.
levels.3: Record each selectable entry, marking which ones appear during ordinary USA play and which remain unused carryovers. Do not claim a hidden track was heard in standard gameplay.

levels.1: An earlier three-board route remains internally but has no menu entry.
levels.2: Treat the retained Beginner course as inaccessible cartridge data, not a normal completion route.
levels.3: Do not modify the completion ROM or invent a button code. Archive the sourced finding that three unused boards remain and require external ROM debugging; normal 100% ends without playing them.
